record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Is there a Borel invariant class C of closed subgroups of S_∞ such that the isomorphism relation on C is not Borel reducible below graph isomorphism? More strongly, can one get an analytic-complete isomorphism relation in this way? The paper asks this in particular for the class of pro-countable groups.

evidence.quote: Problem 22. Is there a Borel, invariant class C of closed subgroups of S∞ with isomorphism relation not Borel below graph isomorphism? Analytic complete? How about the class C of pro-countable groups?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S_\infty$ denote the Polish group of all permutations of $\mathbb{N}$, equipped with the topology of pointwise convergence. The closed subgroups of $S_\infty$ form a standard Borel space (e.g., via the Effros Borel structure on $F(S_\infty)$), on which $S_\infty$ acts by conjugation; topological group isomorphism between closed subgroups of $S_\infty$ coincides on this space with the orbit equivalence relation of an associated $S_\infty$-action, and is in general an analytic equivalence relation. A class $\mathcal{C}$ of closed subgroups of $S_\infty$ is called Borel and invariant if it is Borel as a subset of this standard Borel space and is closed under topological group isomorphism. The graph isomorphism equivalence relation $\cong_{\mathrm{Gr}}$ is the isomorphism relation on the Polish space of countable graphs on $\mathbb{N}$; it is known to be Borel complete among isomorphism relations of countable structures.

Questions:
(a) Does there exist a Borel invariant class $\mathcal{C}$ of closed subgroups of $S_\infty$ such that the topological group isomorphism relation restricted to $\mathcal{C}$ is not Borel reducible to $\cong_{\mathrm{Gr}}$?
(b) Can such a class $\mathcal{C}$ be chosen so that the isomorphism relation on $\mathcal{C}$ is analytic-complete (i.e., every analytic equivalence relation Borel reduces to it)?
(c) Specifically, do (a) or (b) hold for $\mathcal{C}$ equal to the class of pro-countable groups (closed subgroups of $S_\infty$ that are inverse limits of countable discrete groups, equivalently the closed subgroups of $S_\infty$ that have a neighborhood basis at the identity consisting of open normal subgroups)?
artifact.status_search_result: The closest related work (Kechris–Nies–Tent on the complexity of topological group isomorphism) shows that for profinite, locally compact, and Roelcke precompact closed subgroups of $S_\infty$ the isomorphism relation is Borel bireducible with countable graph isomorphism, and gives graph isomorphism as an upper bound for oligomorphic groups. None of the sources located resolve whether some Borel invariant class of closed subgroups of $S_\infty$—and in particular the class of pro-countable groups—has isomorphism relation strictly above graph isomorphism or analytic-complete. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The complexity of topological group isomorphism (Kechris, Nies, Tent)
status_evidence.snippet: For profinite, locally compact, and Roelcke precompact groups, the isomorphism complexity matches countable graph isomorphism; for oligomorphic groups, graph isomorphism is an upper bound but not known to be sharp.
status_evidence.claim: Existing results bound or match graph isomorphism on standard subclasses but do not exhibit a Borel invariant class above graph isomorphism.

status_evidence.title: KechrisNiesTent — subgroups of S_infty
status_evidence.snippet: Studies isomorphism for natural classes of closed subgroups of S_infty within the framework of Borel reducibility.
status_evidence.claim: Authoritative reference on the topic; does not provide a class with isomorphism not Borel reducible to graph isomorphism.
